summary: Heavy stop-out day — NVDA, AMZN, CRWD, and GLD all closed below their daily-close stops on the June 6 session as 30Y pressure and hot-NFP interpretation overwhelmed AI-capex and safe-haven positioning; Short AVGO hit Target 1 at $385. Iran-Israel overnight missile exchange raises Brent above $97; three new ideas added: Short QQQ (fade the pre-CPI NQ bounce), Long MRVL (S&P 500 inclusion June 22 + Jensen $2B halo), and Long USO (Iran-Israel Brent $97+ crude tail hedge).

closed_today.note: NVDA closed $204.04 on June 6, below the $210 daily-close stop. Broad semis (AMD -10.86%, TSM -6.69%) dragged NVDA through the stop despite MRVL/AI-specific Monday bounce.
AMZN closed $245.73 on June 6, below the $248 stop. Macro regime (30Y >5%, Brent >$97, SPCX supply drain) compressed consumer/cloud multiples.
CRWD closed $671.02 on June 5, below the $680 stop. Billings miss (-18% YoY vs 22%+ consensus) proved structural, not timing. The June 25 split record date remains a potential re-entry catalyst.

GLD closed ~$397 (gold ~$4,366/oz) on June 6, well below the $422 stop. Hot-NFP interpretation (172K payrolls) strengthened the USD and pushed real yields higher, overwhelming the Iran geopolitical safe-haven bid.

AVGO closed at $385 on June 6, hitting Target 1 ($385). The June 4 intraday recovery from $413 to $479 was a false floor; institutional selling in Phase 2 of the guidance-plateau repricing brought AVGO to the first demand band.
